input.content:
You are building a frozen evidence-source packet for a focused PFAS treatment
review. Use Web Search to locate independent primary studies, pilot or field
deployments, or quantitative modeling/life-cycle studies that directly address
the task. The defining review is held out and is an exclusion target, not an
evidence source.

Search broadly and return every independently verified eligible primary source
found within the requested candidate-screening ceiling. There is no fixed final
source count and no penalty for retaining multiple eligible studies that address
similar evidence categories. Continue searching across distinct formulations
until the ceiling is reached or additional searches yield no new eligible
sources. Order retained sources from strongest and most complementary to
weakest. Favor sources that collectively cover all task components and preserve PFAS identity,
water matrix, concentration or loading, operating conditions, scale, endpoint,
quantitative result, limitations, residuals, energy, and cost where available.
Review articles and perspectives may help discovery but must not appear in the
  source packet.

For every retained source:

- provide the exact URL inspected by Web Search, matching the URL surfaced by
  the search tool rather than substituting a different repository or index;
- provide a DOI when one is stated by the inspected source;
- identify the publication year and publication status conservatively;
- identify the access scope conservatively;
- include only short evidence passages actually visible in the inspected
  source, each with a stable local locator_id;
- mark a passage verbatim only when it is copied exactly; otherwise mark it as
  a paraphrase;
- never turn a search-result snippet into study evidence; and
- leave unsupported fields empty rather than infer them.

Prefer peer-reviewed articles. Use a preprint, conference abstract, or report
only when it supplies distinct task-relevant evidence unavailable from a
peer-reviewed source, and label its status explicitly.

Do not cite, reconstruct, or use the held-out review. Source and locator IDs are
temporary capture identifiers and will be deterministically renumbered after
validation. Return one JSON object following the supplied schema exactly.

Focused review task:
{"review_brief":"Prepare a focused review of the evidence needed to choose among regeneration, replacement, and end-of-life management for PFAS-loaded adsorption media.","task_id":"RT03","title":"Deciding whether to regenerate or replace PFAS adsorption media"}

Required components:
[{"component_id":"RT03-C1","requirement":"Compare regeneration approaches by PFAS release or destruction, recovered capacity, repeated-cycle performance, and material deterioration."},{"component_id":"RT03-C2","requirement":"Account for liquid, gaseous, or solid residuals and distinguish transfer of PFAS from actual destruction."},{"component_id":"RT03-C3","requirement":"Evaluate the operational, energy, chemical, cost, and sustainability evidence needed for a site-specific decision."}]

Task-specific extraction objective:
Extract adsorbent and PFAS identity, loading protocol, regeneration or disposal method, operating conditions, desorption or destruction endpoint, capacity recovery, cycle number, material change, residual streams, energy, chemicals, and cost.

Held-out anchor identifiers:
{"all_blocked_dois":["10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138"],"all_blocked_titles":["a review of pfas adsorption from aqueous solutions current approaches engineering applications challenges and opportunities"],"all_blocked_urls":["https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138"],"anchor_id":"AR-LEI-2023","corpus_source":"2023 - Lei - A review of PFAS adsorption from aqueous solutions - Current approaches, engineering applications, challenges, and opportunities.pdf","doi":"10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138","title":"A review of PFAS adsorption from aqueous solutions: Current approaches, engineering applications, challenges, and opportunities","url":"https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138"}

Maximum eligible primary sources to inspect and return:
20

Minimum retained sources required for a usable review packet:
6

Search for and inspect independent primary sources. Do not stop after reaching
the minimum. Return every eligible nonduplicate source found before the search
ceiling or evidence-search saturation, after checking the exclusion list and
source type.

search_notes: Search focused on primary studies and modeling/LCA directly relevant to regeneration, replacement, and end-of-life management of PFAS-loaded adsorption media, excluding broad reviews and guidance documents, as required.

Within the 20-source ceiling, 14 distinct primary or modeling studies were retained that collectively address multiple regeneration technologies (solvent/acid, hot water, mixed organic/inorganic, supercritical CO2, microwave, hydrothermal alkaline treatment, and thermal reactivation/incineration), ion-exchange versus GAC performance and regeneration, and leaching/end-of-life behavior of spent media.

Several additional promising references (e.g., detailed thermal mineralization studies, electro-regeneration reviews, landfill-focused PFAS release mechanisms) were identified but either lacked accessible primary data within the inspected pages or overlapped strongly with the retained sources; they were therefore not included to maintain focus on directly task-relevant primary evidence.

sources.citation: Liu B., Chen J., You Y., Sun M. Cyclic removal and destruction of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances from water using ion exchange, resin regeneration, and UV/sulfite reduction. Water Research. 2025;272:122915.
source_limitations: Only abstract and highlights were accessible; detailed operating conditions (column dimensions, flow rates, energy demand for UV/sulfite and distillation, full mass balance of fluoride and byproducts) are not available from the inspected page.
Information on resin physical deterioration, long-term (>3 cycles) performance, and detailed cost/energy analysis is limited in the abstract.
sources.title: Cyclic removal and destruction of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances from water using ion exchange, resin regeneration, and UV/sulfite reduction

sources.citation: Godiya C.B., Ren Z., Minofar B., Leiviskä T. Cyclic sorption/regeneration of ion exchange resins and UV/sulfite treatment for complete perfluorooctane sulfonate removal. Chemical Engineering Journal. 2025;522:167008.
source_limitations: Full-text PDF is linked but the contents were not directly parsed in the inspected view; quantitative data on regeneration efficiency, PFOS desorption kinetics, and capacity recovery over multiple cycles are not captured here.
Details on UV/sulfite operating conditions, energy use, and fluoride/byproduct yields must be obtained from the full article.
sources.title: Cyclic sorption/regeneration of ion exchange resins and UV/sulfite treatment for complete perfluorooctane sulfonate removal

sources.citation: Al-Qaraghuli Y.H., Suri R., Fuller M.E., McKenzie E.R. From solubility to efficiency: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) regeneration from anion exchange resins. Science of the Total Environment. 2025;964:178571.
source_limitations: Only abstract content was inspected; no direct data on PFAS loadings, exact regenerant compositions beyond general solvent and salt types, or quantitative capacity recovery for each cycle are visible.
Information on residual PFAS concentrations in regenerant streams, subsequent handling of regenerant, and energy or cost of regeneration is not available from the abstract page.
sources.title: From solubility to efficiency: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) regeneration from anion exchange resins

sources.citation: Authors not fully listed in inspected excerpt. Supercritical CO2 regeneration of spent ion exchange resins and regenerant destruction – towards zero PFAS waste. ChemRxiv / Cambridge Open Engage preprint. 2024.
source_limitations: Preprint status; peer-review outcome is unknown.

Although the PDF was accessible, detailed cycle-by-cycle adsorption capacity data, PFAS speciation in SCWO effluent, and explicit energy balances for scCO2 and SCWO systems were not fully extracted in this capture.
The study focuses on PFOA-loaded resins; generalization to broader PFAS mixtures and field matrices may be limited.
sources.title: Supercritical CO2 regeneration of spent ion exchange resins and regenerant destruction – towards zero PFAS waste

sources.citation: Gagliano E., Falciglia P.P., Zaker Y., Karanfil T., Roccaro P. Microwave regeneration of granular activated carbon saturated with PFAS. Water Research. 2021;198:117121.
source_limitations: The HERO abstract does not report numerical regeneration efficiencies, PFAS desorption fractions, or PFAS mass balance in off-gas or condensate streams.
No direct information on PFAS destruction vs volatilization, off-gas treatment, or energy consumption per unit GAC mass is available from the inspected abstract.
sources.title: Microwave regeneration of granular activated carbon saturated with PFAS

sources.citation: Ranjbar E., Ahmadi F., Baghdadi M. Regeneration of perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) loaded granular activated carbon using organic/inorganic mixed solutions. Chemical Engineering Science. 2024;300:120623.
source_limitations: Only abstract content was captured; specific PFOS loadings, regeneration efficiencies per cycle, and breakthrough curves after regeneration are not visible.

The fate of PFOS during regeneration (complete recovery in liquid phase vs partial degradation), composition and volume of regenerant waste, and any cost or energy evaluation are not provided in the inspected abstract.
sources.title: Regeneration of perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) loaded granular activated carbon using organic/inorganic mixed solutions

sources.citation: Wang W., Du Z., Deng S., Vakili M., Ren L., Meng P., et al. Regeneration of PFOS loaded activated carbon by hot water and subsequent aeration enrichment of PFOS from eluent. Carbon. 2018;134:199–206.
source_limitations: Only abstract text was accessed; detailed adsorption capacities before and after regeneration, GAC structural characterization, and any decline in capacity across cycles are not visible.
The study recovers PFOS into a concentrated liquid; no destructive treatment or lifecycle analysis of this concentrate is provided on the inspected page.
sources.title: Regeneration of PFOS loaded activated carbon by hot water and subsequent aeration enrichment of PFOS from eluent

sources.citation: Authors not fully listed in inspected excerpt. Regeneration of PFAS-laden granular activated carbon by modified supercritical CO2 extraction. Journal not clearly identified in snippet (PFAS, PFOA, GAC regeneration, supercritical CO2). ~2024.
source_limitations: Access to the full PMC article content was blocked by a reCAPTCHA; only short snippets from the page preview were visible.

Quantitative breakthrough curves before and after regeneration, assessment of GAC property changes, PFAS mass balance in CO2 and co-solvent phases, and energy/cost comparisons to thermal reactivation are not available from the inspected snippets.
sources.title: Regeneration of PFAS-laden granular activated carbon by modified supercritical CO2 extraction

sources.citation: Sun R., Challa S.P., Alinezhad A., Xiao F. Sorptive removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in organic-free water, surface water, and landfill leachate and thermal reactivation of spent sorbents. Journal of Hazardous Materials Advances. 2023;10(2):100311.
source_limitations: The ResearchGate viewer indicates a full-text PDF, but only partial text was directly captured; detailed thermal reactivation conditions (temperature, atmosphere, duration) and quantitative capacity recovery across cycles are not fully extracted.
Information on PFAS destruction vs volatilization during reactivation and on residual PFAS in off-gas or ash is limited in the accessible text.
sources.title: Sorptive removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in organic-free water, surface water, and landfill leachate and thermal reactivation of spent sorbents

sources.citation: Woodard S., Berry J., Newman B. Ion exchange resin for PFAS removal and pilot test comparison to GAC. Remediation. 2017;27(3):19–27.
source_limitations: While the full PDF is accessible, detailed regenerant composition, regeneration frequency, solvent recovery, and management of PFAS-rich regenerant streams are not summarized in the abstract section captured here.
The paper focuses on PFOS and PFOA; information on short-chain PFAS behavior during regeneration is limited. Energy use and cost analyses are not explicitly provided.
sources.title: Ion exchange resin for PFAS removal and pilot test comparison to GAC

sources.citation: DiStefano R., Feliciano T., Mimna R.A., Redding A.M., Matthis J. Thermal destruction of PFAS during full-scale reactivation of PFAS-laden granular activated carbon. Remediation. 2022;32(4):231–238.
source_limitations: Only abstract-level and summary snippets were accessible; detailed furnace temperature profiles, gas residence times, and PFAS speciation in off-gas and residual solids are not captured here.

The study focuses on full-scale reactivation with appropriate off-gas treatment; it does not provide a comparative life-cycle cost or energy analysis versus alternative disposal options in the inspected text.
sources.title: Thermal destruction of PFAS during full-scale reactivation of PFAS-laden granular activated carbon

sources.citation: Lin Z., Doudrick K., Herckes P., Chester M., Westerhoff P., Boyer T.H. Life cycle assessment of the thermal oxidation and pyrolysis of granular activated carbon loaded with perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS). Journal of Cleaner Production. 2025;501:145325.
source_limitations: Only the abstract and highlights were available; detailed inventory data (energy, reagents, emissions) and assumptions about regeneration performance and PFOS mineralization are not visible.

The LCA uses PFOS mineralization data from prior experimental work and assumes 100 % regeneration and post-performance of GAC; uncertainties around these assumptions are not detailed in the inspected text.
sources.title: Life cycle assessment of the thermal oxidation and pyrolysis of granular activated carbon loaded with perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS)

sources.citation: Soker O., Tajdini B., Abarca-Perez A., Strathmann T.J., et al. Reuse of spent granular activated carbon for PFAS removal following hydrothermal alkaline treatment. Water Research. 2025;283:123794.
source_limitations: Only the abstract was inspected; specific PFAS concentrations, destruction and defluorination extents in HALT reactor effluent, and detailed energy and chemical consumption are not visible.
The study focuses on long-chain PFAS; behavior of short-chain PFAS during HALT and potential formation of fluorinated byproducts are not fully described in the abstract.
sources.title: Reuse of spent granular activated carbon for PFAS removal following hydrothermal alkaline treatment

sources.citation: (Authors not fully listed in snippet). Analyzing the release of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances from spent granular activated carbons by standard leaching procedures. Environmental Science & Technology. 2024;58(?):acs.est.4c12093.
source_limitations: Access to the full ACS article was blocked (403), so only brief summary text was captured via search results; specific leaching test conditions, PFAS release rates, and dependence on pH or ionic strength are not available.
The study focuses on leaching behavior in standardized tests, not on regeneration or destruction; no lifecycle cost or energy assessment is visible in the inspected content.
sources.title: Analyzing the release of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances from spent granular activated carbons by standard leaching procedures

sources.citation: Wang W., Du Z., Deng S., et al. Regeneration of PFOS loaded activated carbon by hot water and subsequent aeration enrichment of PFOS from eluent. Carbon. 2018;134:199–206. (EPA HERO summary).
source_limitations: The HERO entry largely mirrors the journal abstract and does not add quantitative performance or detailed operating conditions beyond what is captured in WEB70; it is retained here as an independent regulatory summary but is redundant for many technical parameters.
sources.title: Regeneration of PFOS loaded activated carbon by hot water and subsequent aeration enrichment of PFOS from eluent (EPA HERO record)
